predecessors.name: Cucuteni–Trypillia culture
predecessors.text: the Odessa and Kirovohrad oblasts, the Cucuteni-Trypillia culture's land on the Southern Bug and Dnieper bend until 3000 BCE

successors.name: Catacomb Culture
successors.text: "succeeded in its western range by the Catacomb culture (2800–2200 BC)"; the Catacomb page: "Pontic steppe"

successors.name: Poltavka Culture
successors.text: "in the eastern range by the Poltavka culture (2700–2100 BC)"; the Poltavka page: "flourished on the Volga-Ural steppe and the forest steppe"

ledger.x: 3400: the Yamnaya culture arises in the Don-Volga steppe.
3200: the early Yamnaya horizon has spread across the Pontic-Caspian steppe.
3000 BCE: the Odessa and Kirovohrad oblasts pass from the Cucuteni-Trypillia culture to the Yamnaya.
2600: the Yamnaya culture gives way to the Catacomb culture in the west and the Poltavka culture in the east.

certainty.note: A steppe culture drawn by modern oblasts and a gazetteer region; every edge is soft, and the page gives no boundary except the three rivers of its lead.
